extracted.intended_audience: state and tribal air agencies, EPA regional offices, power plant owners/operators, reliability authorities, and other regulated stakeholders and commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble and regulatory guidance implementing Clean Air Act section 111 standards and emission guidelines for fossil fuel-fired electric utility generating units (EGUs), including programmatic requirements for state plans, reliability flexibilities, environmental justice considerations, and procedural requirements for applicability and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability emergency mechanism (existing and new sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: For existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs, a short-term reliability emergency mechanism is available for states to provide more flexibility by using an alternative emission limitation during acute operational emergencies when the grid might be temporarily under heavy strain. A similar short-term reliability emergency mechanism is also available to new sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism allows affected EGUs to operate at baseline emission rates during documented reliability emergencies. Use requires appropriate documentation of emergency conditions (see section XII.F). Intended as a limited, short-term tool to address acute operational emergencies without undermining long-term compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance-date extension for CCS implementation (up to 1 year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option for states to provide for a compliance date extension for existing sources of up to 1 year under certain circumstances for sources that are installing control technologies to comply with their standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are for circumstances outside an owner/operator's control (e.g., supply chain challenges or permitting delays). To utilize this pathway there must be an adequate demonstration of need and certification by a reliability authority, and approval by the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator. Any extensions exceeding 1 year must be addressed through a state plan revision. For extension requests exceeding 6 months, the EPA plans to seek the advice of FERC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism (delay planned cease-operation dates up to 1 year)
rubrics_metrics.description: States may provide, by inclusion in their state plans, a reliability assurance mechanism of up to 1 year that under limited circumstances would allow existing units that had planned to cease operating by a certain date to temporarily remain available to support reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is limited in scope and duration (up to 1 year) and requires a documented and verified reliability concern, adequate demonstration of need, certification by a reliability authority, and approval by the EPA Regional Administrator. Extensions beyond 1 year require a state plan revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for baseload new combustion turbines to request CCS extension (1 year)
rubrics_metrics.description: For new fossil fuel-fired combustion turbines, a mechanism is created whereby baseload units may request a 1-year extension of their CCS compliance deadline under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must demonstrate the circumstances warranting the extension; the preamble explains analogous requirements for demonstration, reliability certification, and Regional Administrator approval (see related reliability-extension guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance timeline extension for unforeseen implementation delays
rubrics_metrics.description: A mechanism to extend compliance timelines by up to 1 year in the case of unforeseen circumstances, outside of an owner/operator's control, that delay the ability to apply controls (e.g., supply chain challenges or permitting delays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide flexibility for unanticipated delays in control technology implementation; approvals require documentation of circumstances and are subject to EPA oversight (see section XII.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent unit-specific compliance information
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for transparent unit-specific compliance information for EGUs to allow grid operators to plan for system changes with greater certainty and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing transparent unit-level compliance schedules and status information is a program feature intended to aid reliability planning by balancing authorities and system operators; further detail in section XII.F.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER evaluation statutory criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER), EPA considered all of the statutory criteria for BSER, including emission reductions, cost, energy requirements, and non-air health and environmental considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory criteria form the framework for evaluating candidate control approaches (e.g., CCS, hydrogen co-firing). Uncertainties or inadequacies in meeting these criteria (e.g., for low-GHG hydrogen co-firing) can preclude finalizing a pathway as part of BSER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Justice analysis and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with Executive Order 14096 and EPA policy, EPA carefully considered impacts on communities with environmental justice (EJ) concerns; conducted extensive outreach with Tribal nations and communities with EJ concerns; and summarized EJ analysis in the preamble and RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA analyzed distributional air quality and public health impacts (e.g., PM2.5 and ozone changes) across demographic groups and geographic areas in the RIA; acknowledges potential for localized increases in emissions from CCS operations and commits to regulatory frameworks (including interagency coordination and permitting guidance) to reduce localized risks and protect public health and the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement requirements for state plan development
rubrics_metrics.description: States must include requirements for meaningful engagement in development of state plans, including engagement with energy workers and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should include energy workers employed at affected EGUs, workers who may construct and install pollution control technology, workers employed by fuel extraction and delivery, organizations representing workers, and communities living near affected EGUs. The preamble references specific meaningful engagement provisions (see section X.E.1.b.i) and notes coordination with Energy Communities IWG resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of stakeholder input in state determinations of EGU operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA expects states, in deciding future operation of existing sources, to consider a number of factors and weigh input from a wide range of potentially affected stakeholders (including community members, energy workers, consumers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States' meaningful engagement requirements are intended to ensure interested stakeholders have opportunity to have concerns heard as states balance standards of performance, compliance strategies, compliance flexibilities, public health, and environmental considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability criteria and dates (NSPS and emission guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines source category and applicability: fossil fuel-fired electric utility generating units (NAICS 221112 and 921150). Final amendments to 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT apply to affected facilities that began construction after Jan 8, 2014 but before May 23, 2023; NSPS in subpart TTTTa apply to facilities that begin construction/reconstruction/modification on or after May 23, 2023. Emission guidelines in subpart UUUUb are for states to develop plans for existing sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains 'existing source' definition under section 111(a)(6), Tribal Authority Rule options for tribes to develop TIPs, and that EPA may establish a Federal plan for facilities in Indian country until a TIP is approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and petition for reconsideration procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 307(b)(1), judicial review is available only by filing a petition for review in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit by July 8, 2024. Under section 307(d)(7)(B), only objections raised with reasonable specificity during the public comment period may be raised during judicial review. Petition for Reconsideration may be convened if impracticable to raise objection during comment period or if grounds arose after but within time for judicial review and are centrally relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for Reconsideration should be submitted to the Office of the Administrator with a copy to the listed contacts and the Associate General Counsel for the Air and Radiation Law Office; separate challenges to requirements are limited as provided in CAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA resource adequacy and capacity expansion modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA evaluated resource adequacy implications in a technical support document and conducted capacity expansion modeling of the final rules in a manner that takes into account resource adequacy needs, concluding resource adequacy can be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling included a scenario that complies with the final rules while meeting resource adequacy, plus sensitivity analyses for higher demand and interactions with other power sector rules. Models and analyses are documented in the TSD and RIA (section 6) and inform the design of compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of local non-GHG impacts and comprehensive sector coverage in future rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA recognizes the need to address emissions from a broader set of stationary combustion turbines and to consider local non-GHG impacts (such as NOx) and reliability/affordability when designing guidelines for existing stationary combustion turbines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency is not finalizing certain proposed guidelines for existing combustion turbines and intends to issue a more comprehensive proposal that accounts for local non-GHG impacts, distributional concerns, and the role of these units for grid reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSR/BACT permitting guidance updates related to CCS
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA plans to review and update guidance on New Source Review (NSR) permitting, specifically regarding Best Available Control Technology (BACT) determinations for GHG emissions and consideration of co-pollutant increases from sources installing CCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of ensuring a robust regulatory framework to reduce risks of localized emissions increases and protect public health; coordination across Federal agencies and with CEQ CCUS guidance is noted.
